findings.passage: “The legislature continues to make election integrity one of our top priorities,” said August.  “I am confident that voters will approve Voter ID overwhelmingly in April.”
findings.note: Press release on the resolutions to put a photo ID requirement for voting into the state constitution; he expects voters to approve it. (The press release page holds the text as an image, https://legis.wisconsin.gov/assembly/31/august/media/marp2njz/voterid2025.jpg; the passage was read from that image.)

findings.passage: “Our goal is to get Voter ID into the constitution so that the common-sense law cannot be blocked by progressive judges.”
findings.note: Same release; he gives his reason for putting the photo ID rule into the constitution. (The press release page holds the text as an image, https://legis.wisconsin.gov/assembly/31/august/media/marp2njz/voterid2025.jpg; the passage was read from that image.)

findings.passage: August pointed out that cementing the popular law into the Constitution will ensure an activist court is unable to strike down the provision.
findings.note: Same release; text written about him in the press release, issued from his office, and not a direct quote. (The press release page holds the text as an image, https://legis.wisconsin.gov/assembly/31/august/media/marp2njz/voterid2025.jpg; the passage was read from that image.)

findings.passage: A key to ensuring election integrity in Wisconsin continues to be the requirement of a photo ID to vote.
findings.note: Legislative e-update by him on election integrity; photo ID to vote section.

findings.passage: Putting this common-sense provision into our constitution will ensure it cannot be ignored or struck down by an activist court.
findings.note: Same e-update, photo ID section.

findings.passage: I authored another constitutional amendment that would affirm that only US citizens are eligible to vote.
findings.note: Same e-update; he says he wrote a constitutional amendment on citizenship as a voting requirement.

findings.passage: This will preempt the disturbing trend around the country where non-citizens are being allowed to vote in elections.
findings.note: Same e-update; his stated reason for the citizenship amendment.

findings.passage: Over the past few years, we've taken action to pass numerous election reforms.
findings.note: Same e-update; introduces a list of other election bills he will keep pushing, including maintaining accurate voter rolls, removing non-citizens from voter rolls, banning ballot harvesting and closing voter ID loopholes (list items are fragments, not copied as a passage).
